title: Generic Enterprise Engineering Standards
description: A vendor-neutral stand-in for an internal engineering standards catalogue: authentication, authorisation, secret handling, observability, dependency hygiene, quality gates. Fork this file and replace the control ids/titles with your own catalogue — that is the supported way to express house rules without hard-coding one company's private standard into the tool.

gate.note: Default enterprise posture: blockers stop the release, highs need a dated, owned exception.

SEC-XSS-DANGEROUS-HTML.title: All rendered untrusted content is escaped or sanitised at the sink

SEC-MARKDOWN-HTML-SINK.title: All rendered untrusted content is escaped or sanitised at the sink
Markup generators used with raw-HTML sinks are allowlist based

SEC-TOKEN-WEBSTORAGE.title: Session material is held in storage unreadable by page script (HttpOnly cookie or in-memory)

SEC-JWT-CLIENT-TRUST.title: Token claims are only trusted after signature verification by a service

SEC-CLIENT-SIDE-AUTHZ.title: Authorisation is enforced server-side; the client may only hide UI

SEC-UNAUTH-HANDLER.title: Every network-exposed handler requires an authenticated principal

SEC-CHILD-PROCESS-SHELL.title: Process execution uses argv arrays, never an interpolated shell string

SEC-PATH-TRAVERSAL.title: Filesystem access derived from request input is confined to a validated root

SEC-SSRF-FETCH.title: Outbound requests to caller-influenced destinations use a destination allowlist

SEC-WEAK-CRYPTO.title: Only approved algorithms and CSPRNGs are used

SEC-TIMING-UNSAFE-COMPARE.title: Secrets and signatures are compared in constant time

SEC-CRYPTO-IV-REUSE.title: Authenticated encryption with a unique per-message nonce

SEC-WEBCRYPTO-MISUSE.title: Only approved algorithms and CSPRNGs are used

SEC-SIGNATURE-VERIFY-DISCARDED.title: Signature verification failures are fatal and cannot be bypassed

SEC-EVAL.title: No dynamic code evaluation of runtime data

SEC-SECRET-IN-CLIENT-BUNDLE.title: No secret value reaches a client-distributed artefact

SEC-CSP-MISSING.title: Web responses set CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and frame-ancestors

SEC-TLS-DISABLED.title: Certificate validation is never disabled outside local development

SEC-CORS-WILDCARD.title: CORS origins are an explicit allowlist

SEC-POSTMESSAGE-ORIGIN.title: Cross-frame messages validate origin on both ends

SEC-TARGET-BLANK.title: External links drop referrer and opener

SEC-SECRET-COMMITTED.title: Secrets live in a managed secret store; source control holds none

DEP-ADVISORY.title: No known high/critical advisory ships in a release
Dependency updates are automated and reviewed

DEP-LICENSE.title: Third-party licences are inventoried and compatible with distribution terms

DOCKER-ROOT.title: Containers run as a non-root user

DOCKER-UNPINNED-BASE.title: Base images are pinned by digest

DOCKER-SECRET-ARG.title: Build arguments carry no secret material

CI-NO-SECURITY-GATE.title: The PR gate runs tests, lint and dependency/secret scanning and fails the build

CI-UNPINNED-ACTION.title: Third-party CI actions are pinned to an immutable commit

CI-RISKY-TRIGGER.title: Workflows with write permissions never run untrusted fork code

QUA-SWALLOWED-CATCH.title: Caught errors are logged or rethrown; never silently discarded

QUA-CONSOLE-LOGGING.title: Structured logging through a single abstraction

QUA-ANY-DENSITY.title: Type escape hatches are rare, reviewed and justified

QUA-FILE-SIZE.title: Modules stay within a reviewable size budget

QUA-TEST-THINNESS.title: Risk-weighted automated test coverage exists for every shipped surface

QUA-TODO-DENSITY.title: Deferred work is tracked in the issue tracker, not in comments
